title: WAL commit-path bundle: disable commit_delay, gate siblings high, engage writer flush batching
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 applies a fixed sleep to nearly every commit (only 5 terminals), adding per-commit stall without coalescing real groups; wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer-side flush batching so WAL writes are not coalesced.
mechanism: The incumbent pays a fixed 100us group-commit sleep on almost every commit because commit_siblings=2 is trivially satisfied by 5 terminals, yet wal_writer_flush_after=0 prevents the WAL writer from batching writes. Setting commit_delay=0 removes the unconditional stall; raising commit_siblings to 20 keeps the (zero) window inactive so no accidental sleep returns; setting wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) lets the WAL writer coalesce background writes, reducing wal_waiting_backends and InsertTweet commit latency without gating foreground commits.
query_effect: InsertTweet commit path loses the fixed 100us sleep and benefits from coalesced WAL writer flushes; GetUserTweets read path unchanged.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful transaction TPS as InsertTweet terminal occupancy drops and commit queueing eases.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 decreases; overall p95 roughly unchanged since GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity.

predictions.rationale: Removing the fixed 100us commit sleep and enabling writer flush batching should cut InsertTweet commit latency.
Writer-side flush batching should reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Freed InsertTweet terminal capacity raises completed transaction goodput.

alternatives.statement: wal_waiting_backends p95=1 is sampling noise and the commit path is not the binding constraint; TPS stays flat.
Larger wal_writer_flush_after delays durability batching and increases InsertTweet tail latency instead of reducing it.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent carries a fixed per-commit sleep (commit_delay=100, commit_siblings=2) that is nearly always active with 5 terminals, plus disabled writer flush batching. Removing the stall and enabling writer-side batching targets the observed wal_wait anomaly without touching the dominant read path.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0 (allowed [0,1000]); removes the fixed per-commit sleep that is active on nearly every commit with 5 terminals.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit collection window; 0 disables the fixed sleep

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe high bound 20 (allowed [0,20]); with 5 terminals, 20 siblings guarantees the (zero) window never activates, preventing accidental stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; high value keeps window inactive

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units = 2MB) within safe [0,1024]; engages writer-side flush batching so background WAL writes coalesce instead of flushing per write.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; batches background WAL writes

nodes.label: Remove fixed per-commit stall; engage writer-side flush batching

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: GetUserTweets dominates 87.6% terminal capacity; read-path latency is the primary TPS lever and is untouched here.
